definition: AI Mode is a search feature used within Google Search.
details: In March 2025, Google introduced an experimental "AI Mode" within its search platform, enabling users to input complex, multi-part queries and receive comprehensive, AI-generated responses. This feature uses Google's Gemini model, which enhances the system's reasoning capabilities and supports multimodal inputs, including text, images, and voice. Users need to be signed in to be able to use the image generation features. Initially, AI Mode was available to Google One AI Premium subscribers in the United States, who could access it through the Search Labs platform. This phased rollout allowed Google to gather user feedback and refine the feature before a broader release.

explainer.lead: AI Mode is an experimental way to use Google Search for complicated questions that would normally take several separate searches. It uses Google's Gemini model to produce a comprehensive response from text, image, or voice input.

tiers.eli5: AI Mode is like asking a librarian one big question with several parts, instead of asking lots of little questions one at a time. You can type, speak, or use pictures, and it puts together a detailed answer. It began as an experiment for a limited group of Google users in the United States.
tiers.practitioner: Use AI Mode through Google Search when a task is better expressed as one complex, multi-part query than as several keyword searches. Its multimodal interface accepts text, images, and voice, but image-generation features require the user to be signed in. During the initial rollout, access required a US Google One AI Premium subscription and Search Labs, so availability and feedback-driven changes were practical considerations.
tiers.paperLevel: AI Mode can be described as f(text, image, voice) -> comprehensive AI-generated search response, with Google's Gemini model providing reasoning for complex, multi-part queries. Google introduced it experimentally in March 2025. Its initial evaluation setting was a phased US rollout through Search Labs to Google One AI Premium subscribers, intended to collect feedback before broader release.

explainer.example: A user could ask one question that compares several holiday destinations, requests a different budget for each, and asks for an itinerary based on those constraints, rather than running a separate search for every part.

usedIn.name: Google Search
usedIn.detail: Provides AI Mode as a search feature for complex, multi-part queries and AI-generated responses.

usedIn.name: Search Labs
usedIn.detail: Hosted initial access for Google One AI Premium subscribers in the United States.

explainer.intuition: Instead of making you break a complicated information need into many searches, AI Mode lets you state the whole request at once. Gemini then helps the search system reason over that request and return one comprehensive response.
howItWorks: Open AI Mode within Google Search.
Enter a complex, multi-part request using text, images, or voice.
The feature uses Gemini's reasoning capabilities to process the request.
Google Search returns a comprehensive, AI-generated response.
explainer.whyItMatters: It changes search from a sequence of narrow queries into a single interaction built around a larger request. The phased rollout also gave Google a way to gather user feedback and refine the experimental feature before wider release.
misconceptions: AI Mode is a feature within Google Search, not the name of the Gemini model it uses.
It was not initially available to every Search user: access began with US Google One AI Premium subscribers through Search Labs.
Its image-generation features require users to be signed in.

diagram.caption: AI Mode accepts multimodal queries in Google Search and uses Gemini to generate a comprehensive response.
